articles.title: Could Aaron Donald still dominate for the Rams? Why an NFL comeback might be more realistic than many think
articles.standfirst: The juggernaut was still one of the best defensive players in football when he retired in 2023
articles.summary: The juggernaut was still one of the best defensive players in football when he retired in 2023
articles.body:
Few questions in football are more fascinating right now than this one: Can Aaron Donald still make an impact if he returns to the NFL? For most retired players, the answer would be easy. A two-year absence from football at age 35 would typically end any discussion about elite-level performance.

Aaron Donald is not most players. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year has become the subject of growing comeback speculation throughout the summer, with reports indicating he has continued training and even worked out with the Los Angeles Rams as he weighs a possible return. Rams head coach Sean McVay has done little to cool the rumors, openly acknowledging that Donald could still be effective if he decided to come back.

The bigger question is whether he could still be Aaron Donald. The strongest argument in favor of a comeback is simple: Donald wasn't declining when he retired. When he walked away following the 2023 season, he was still one of the best defensive players in football.

He finished that year with eight sacks, earned another Pro Bowl selection, and was named First-Team All-Pro for the eighth time in his career. Most NFL legends retire because their bodies no longer allow them to perform at a high level.

Donald retired because he no longer wanted the grind

Reports throughout 2026 have suggested that Donald has remained in excellent shape and has continued on-field work while considering a return. Multiple NFL insiders have described a comeback as a legitimate possibility rather than a publicity stunt. And if he returns, he would be stepping into perhaps the most favorable situation of his career.

Myles Garrett changes everything. During Donald's prime, opposing offenses often built entire game plans around stopping him. Now imagine offensive coordinators trying to handle Donald and Myles Garrett on the same defensive front. The Rams' blockbuster acquisition of Garrett has dramatically altered the equation. Sean McVay recently joked that if Donald decides to "dust them off" at age 35, he could still perform "at a pretty high clip."

He's probably right. Donald would no longer need to be the centerpiece of every defensive game plan. Garrett's presence would create one-on-one opportunities that Donald rarely enjoyed during his first stint in Los Angeles. For the first time in years, Donald might actually face fewer double teams than the players around him. That's a terrifying thought for quarterbacks.

Of course, there are legitimate reasons for caution because football is different from training. Donald has not played in an NFL game since the Rams' playoff loss following the 2023 season. By the time he takes the field again, nearly three years will have passed since his last meaningful snap.

History is not especially kind to players returning after multi-year retirements. The physical demands of playing defensive tackle are immense. Conditioning can be rebuilt. Timing, reaction speed, and the ability to withstand constant collisions are much harder to replicate outside of live competition.

Even supporters of a comeback acknowledge that expecting the 2018 version of Aaron Donald would be unrealistic. The player who once routinely posted double-digit sacks while facing constant double teams may not exist anymore. But that doesn't mean he can't still be highly effective.

The Rams don't need Donald to be the best defensive player in football. They need him to be a productive one. Even if Donald returns at 80 percent of his peak level, he would likely remain one of the better interior defensive linemen in the NFL . His technique, leverage, football intelligence, and hand usage have always separated him from other players. Those skills don't disappear overnight.

articles.title: How Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant helped Myles Garrett develop ‘killer instinct’ on the field
articles.standfirst: The Rams star explained why Bryant’s ruthless approach still influences how he prepares to dominate NFL opponents
articles.summary: The Rams star explained why Bryant’s ruthless approach still influences how he prepares to dominate NFL opponents
articles.body:
Myles Garrett has spent his career terrorizing NFL quarterbacks, but the mindset behind that dominance was shaped partly by an athlete who made his name on a basketball court in Los Angeles.

Now preparing for his first season with the Los Angeles Rams , Garrett has revealed how Lakers legend Kobe Bryant became one of the sporting figures he studied while developing the mentality that helped turn him into one of football’s most feared defenders.

Appearing on “Boardroom Talks,” Garrett grouped Bryant alongside NFL icon Lawrence Taylor and NBA great Michael Jordan as athletes whose competitive instincts separated them from everyone around them.

“You get to see the duality of it,” Garrett said. “You have [Lawrence Taylor], you have Kobe, you have [Michael Jordan], who have a killer instinct. It exudes from them. They want to kill you, want to take you out the game.”

Bryant built his reputation around that relentless competitive approach during 20 seasons with the Lakers. His “Mamba Mentality” became shorthand for obsessive preparation, resilience and an unwillingness to accept anything below his own standards.

Garrett believes that same combination of aggression and freedom can be transferred to football.

Kobe Bryant mentality left mark on Garrett

“Just playing the game as freely as you can, trying to combine the two,” Garrett said. “That’s how I feel like I walk on the field. I walk on the field and I plan to destroy the game, but I plan to have fun doing it the whole time.”

Bryant ’s career provided countless examples of that mentality. He won five NBA championships, became an 18-time All-Star and twice led the league in scoring.

One of his most memorable displays of toughness came in 2013, when he remained on the court long enough to make two free throws after suffering a torn Achilles.

Three years later, Bryant closed his career by scoring 60 points against the Utah Jazz in his final game at Staples Center.

Garrett also pointed to Muhammad Ali as another major influence, particularly because of the heavyweight champion’s ability to defeat opponents psychologically as well as physically.

“Once you start playing those mental games and doing that mental gymnastics, you’re already defeated,” Garrett said. “Then he’s got you right where he wants you.”

Those influences help explain the mentality Garrett is now bringing to Los Angeles.

Rams hope Garrett’s mentality leads to Super Bowl

The Rams acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns during the offseason after another remarkable individual campaign in which he recorded 23 sacks, surpassing Michael Strahan ’s long-standing single-season record.

His introduction to Los Angeles has been deliberately cautious, however, with knee soreness limiting his participation throughout training camp.

“I feel good,” Garrett said earlier in August. “I'm allowed to get sore. I'm a little old.”

Head coach Sean McVay has insisted the Rams are prioritizing Garrett ’s availability for the regular season rather than pushing him through meaningless preseason work.

“We are, yeah,” McVay said when asked whether Los Angeles was being cautious. “The goal is, what can we do to be able to get him ready to roll for Australia? That's kind of where you see that approach.”

Garrett has already conquered most individual challenges available to an NFL pass rusher. The next one is considerably bigger.

Los Angeles brought him in to help chase a Super Bowl, and Garrett appears ready to attack that objective with a mentality borrowed from one of the city’s greatest sporting icons.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Alert: Possible suspension of Puka Nacua on the Rams could be major problem
articles.standfirst: A potential suspension creates risk around the Rams receiver
articles.summary: A potential suspension creates risk around the Rams receiver
articles.body:
Puka Nacua ’s fantasy value has become one of the trickiest calls of draft season, not because anything has changed about his talent, but because managers still don't know whether he will be available when the Los Angeles Rams open the NFL regular season.

Nacua is coming off a dominant year in which he led the NFL with 129 receptions, finished second with 1,715 receiving yards and scored 10 touchdowns. That production made him fantasy football’s No.1 wide receiver.

Normally, those numbers would make him an easy first-round selection. The complication is the possibility of NFL discipline stemming from several off-field matters that remain under review.

No suspension has been announced, but ESPN insider Adam Schefter made clear earlier this month that missing the opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia remains possible.

“[Nacua] could potentially face discipline for some of the offseason headlines that accompanied him,” Schefter said.

He added: “It’s possible that when the 49ers and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game.”

That uncertainty should matter in fantasy drafts. It shouldn't, however, trigger a collapse in Nacua ’s value.

Short suspension would barely dent Nacua’s upside

Fantasy managers should separate the risk of a suspension from the severity of one.

If Nacua misses only Week 1, his season-long value remains extremely strong. Passing on a player capable of delivering 1,700 receiving yards because of a single absence could end up being an overreaction.

Even a two-game suspension wouldn't necessarily push him outside the first round. The calculation changes if the NFL announces something more significant.

A four-game absence would make Nacua much harder to justify among the top three or four overall selections, particularly when Ja’Marr Chase and other elite receivers offer similar ceilings without the same availability concern.

Until there is clarity, the safest approach is to move Nacua down a few spots rather than several rounds.

If he reaches the back half of Round 1, the value becomes much easier to defend. If nervous managers allow him to fall into Round 2, the risk may be worth embracing.

Fantasy managers should build around uncertainty

Anyone drafting Nacua should have a contingency plan. Using another early selection on a reliable wide receiver can protect against a short-term absence and prevent a roster from becoming too dependent on one player.

Davante Adams is another major weapon in the Rams offense, while Los Angeles’ decision to bring Tutu Atwell back has created further speculation about Nacua’s status. That move alone, though, isn't evidence that a suspension is imminent.

Nacua remains one of the most dangerous fantasy assets on the board. The smartest move is not to pretend the suspension risk does not exist. It is to price that risk correctly.

Until the NFL announces significant discipline, Nacua still belongs in the first-round conversation. If he slips much further, the uncertainty could turn into somebody else’s best draft-night bargain.

articles.title: Rams' Aaron Donald's two-word message to Commissioner Roger Goodell should terrify the rest of the NFL
articles.standfirst: Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season, with another Super Bowl ring in mind.
articles.summary: Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season, with another Super Bowl ring in mind.
articles.body:
It's official: Aaron Donald has unretired and is once again a member of the Los Angeles Rams . Donald's return had been teased nearly all offseason, but it finally came to fruition with the season less than two weeks way.

Donald will join Myles Garrett , Matthew Stafford , Puka Nacua , and more stars on a truly stacked Rams roster. At this point, Los Angeles is the overwhelming favorite to win the Super Bowl . Whether that happens or not, though, Donald coming back and dominating at age 35 after over two years out of football would be truly special.

Aaron Donald channels Michael Jordan in return statement

For those doubting whether Donald can do that, his physique in workout videos should say enough. But in case they don't, Donald made sure to make a short but strong statement on the day of his return . He sent a message indicating his return to the NFL to Commissioner Roger Goodell with only two words: " I'm Back ".

Donald marked his return with his first official practice as a Rams member later in the day. The defensive lineman kept things relatively simple, running light drills . It was a walkthrough day for the Rams , although Donald probably wouldn't have gone full blast even if it wasn't.

The Rams ended up giving Donald a one-year contract worth $20 million , that could go all the way up to $30 million with incentives . If it does go all the way up, it means Donald returned to his usual self this season, which would be a major win for the Rams.

articles.title: Aaron Donald's wife reveals surprising reason behind his Rams comeback
articles.standfirst: Family played a major role in the Rams legend's unexpected return.
articles.summary: Family played a major role in the Rams legend's unexpected return.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald's return to the Los Angeles Rams came as a surprise across the NFL, but his wife Erica has now revealed that the decision was driven by something far more personal than unfinished business on the field.

Donald had stepped away from football after the 2023 season, ending a Hall-of-Fame-level career that included three Defensive Player of the Year awards and a Super Bowl title.

But after spending time away from the game, the former defensive tackle ultimately decided he still wanted another chapter with Los Angeles.

Aaron Donald's family helped change his mind

Erica Donald explained that retirement gave her husband something he hadn't experienced much during his playing career: extended time at home with his family.

"He got a chance to really be a dad," she said.

That time away appears to have changed his perspective rather than completely satisfying his desire to remain retired.

According to Erica , the family became an important part of the conversation when Donald began considering a comeback.

"The kids were like, 'Dad, we want to see you play,'" she said.

That reaction helped push Donald toward returning to the Rams , where he had spent his entire NFL career before retiring.

Rams legend still had football left in him

Erica also made clear that Donald hadn't completely lost his competitive edge during retirement.

"He missed football," she said.

The combination of family encouragement and his own desire to compete again eventually became enough to bring him back.

Donald had previously spoken about wanting to leave the game while still physically capable of performing at an elite level rather than waiting until his body forced him out.

His return now gives the Rams one of the most dominant defensive players of his generation back in the middle of their front.

There will naturally be questions about how quickly Donald can regain his previous level after time away, but the motivation behind the comeback appears clear.

This wasn't simply about chasing another contract or adding to an already remarkable resume.

Donald had spent retirement enjoying life as a father, but when his children told him they wanted to watch him play again, it helped reopen a door many assumed had been permanently closed.

articles.title: Gisele Bundchen gets dragged back into NFL debate after Aaron Donald's Rams return
articles.standfirst: Aaron Donald's comeback unexpectedly revived comparisons with Tom Brady's retirement saga.
articles.summary: Aaron Donald's comeback unexpectedly revived comparisons with Tom Brady's retirement saga.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald's return to the Los Angeles Rams has unexpectedly dragged Gisele Bundchen back into the NFL conversation years after her divorce from Tom Brady .

The three-time Defensive Player of the Year came out of retirement after agreeing to a one-year, $20 million deal with the Rams .

His wife, Erica Donald , immediately celebrated the decision on social media.

"I let him out of the house y'all," Erica wrote alongside laughing and heart emojis.

That prompted NFL insider Clarence Hill Jr . to make a pointed comparison with Brady's former marriage.

"If only Gisele Bundchen had been equally supportive," Hill wrote.

Gisele Bundchen gets pulled back into old Tom Brady debate

The comment reopened discussion around Brady's brief 2022 retirement and subsequent return to football.

Brady initially retired saying he wanted to spend more time with his family, only to reverse the decision six weeks later.

Bundchen publicly supported Brady , but she later expressed concerns about his return to the NFL. Reports also emerged that the couple were experiencing marital problems before they filed for divorce in October 2022.

That history made Hill's comparison inevitable, although Donald's situation appears very different.

Aaron Donald credits wife Erica for comeback

Donald made clear that his own return wouldn't have happened without his wife's approval.

"I think my wife played a huge part in this, me making this decision, period," Donald said. "Because, if the wife wasn't happy, it wasn't gonna get done. We gotta make sure that the household was good. The kid was okay with it all, having them hard conversations, figuring things out. What I wanted to do, if I was gonna do it, how would we do it."

He said Erica ultimately gave him her full backing.

"So, my wife was onboard. She said, 'If you wanna do this, just put your 100%.' ... She played a huge part in me figuring this out because it really wasn't an easy decision."

Donald first met Erica in 2015 while she was working for the Rams, and the couple later married privately.

His comeback may belong entirely to the Donald family, but one social media comparison was enough to bring Bundchen and Brady's old retirement drama back into the NFL spotlight.

articles.title: Trouble for the Rams: Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett could miss Week 1
articles.standfirst: Los Angeles wants Garrett ready for Australia, but the team is taking no chances with his knee
articles.summary: Los Angeles wants Garrett ready for Australia, but the team is taking no chances with his knee
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams built their defense around the idea of unleashing Myles Garrett alongside Aaron Donald . With the season opener approaching, however, the first question is whether Garrett will be ready to take the field at all.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has spent much of the summer managing swelling in his knee and has been a full participant in practice only twice.

That has made his status one of the biggest storylines surrounding Los Angeles ahead of its Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Sean McVay has now provided the clearest indication yet of what the Rams are working toward.

“He’s making good progress. Really good progress,” McVay said Monday. “The goal all along has been Australia.”

Garrett ’s limited practice work has naturally created concern, especially after the Rams expected him to return last week and he remained sidelined.

McVay , though, has continued to frame the situation as caution rather than setback.

Rams not willing to gamble Garrett’s season

Garrett arrived in Los Angeles after leading the NFL with 23 sacks in 2025, and the Rams paid heavily to acquire one of the league’s most dominant defensive players.

That makes the temptation to get him on the field immediately obvious.

McVay insists the organization will not allow the excitement surrounding the opener to override Garrett ’s long-term health.

“If he’s not ready, and that’s not what’s best for him and the team, absolutely wouldn’t have him play in Australia,” McVay said.

That approach makes sense for a player expected to anchor the defense over an entire season rather than simply provide a spectacle in Week 1.

The Rams also named Garrett one of their captains, underlining how quickly he has become a central figure despite missing considerable practice time.

Donald’s return adds more uncertainty

The intrigue has only increased following Donald ’s decision to come out of retirement.

The prospect of Garrett and Donald lining up together has immediately transformed expectations for the Rams ’ defensive front, but Donald is also being eased back after two seasons away from football.

He didn't practice Monday, instead working in the weight room as part of what the team described as a planned progression.

That means Los Angeles could enter the opener without either of the two names generating the most excitement around its defense.

The Rams are clearly hoping it does not come to that. Garrett is trending in the right direction, and McVay ’s comments make Australia the obvious target.

paragraphs: The Los Angeles Rams built their defense around the idea of unleashing Myles Garrett alongside Aaron Donald . With the season opener approaching, however, the first question is whether Garrett will be ready to take the field at all.
The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has spent much of the summer managing swelling in his knee and has been a full participant in practice only twice.
That has made his status one of the biggest storylines surrounding Los Angeles ahead of its Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.
Sean McVay has now provided the clearest indication yet of what the Rams are working toward.
“He’s making good progress. Really good progress,” McVay said Monday. “The goal all along has been Australia.”
Garrett ’s limited practice work has naturally created concern, especially after the Rams expected him to return last week and he remained sidelined.
McVay , though, has continued to frame the situation as caution rather than setback.
Rams not willing to gamble Garrett’s season
Garrett arrived in Los Angeles after leading the NFL with 23 sacks in 2025, and the Rams paid heavily to acquire one of the league’s most dominant defensive players.
That makes the temptation to get him on the field immediately obvious.
McVay insists the organization will not allow the excitement surrounding the opener to override Garrett ’s long-term health.
“If he’s not ready, and that’s not what’s best for him and the team, absolutely wouldn’t have him play in Australia,” McVay said.
That approach makes sense for a player expected to anchor the defense over an entire season rather than simply provide a spectacle in Week 1.
The Rams also named Garrett one of their captains, underlining how quickly he has become a central figure despite missing considerable practice time.
Donald’s return adds more uncertainty
The intrigue has only increased following Donald ’s decision to come out of retirement.

The prospect of Garrett and Donald lining up together has immediately transformed expectations for the Rams ’ defensive front, but Donald is also being eased back after two seasons away from football.
He didn't practice Monday, instead working in the weight room as part of what the team described as a planned progression.
That means Los Angeles could enter the opener without either of the two names generating the most excitement around its defense.
The Rams are clearly hoping it does not come to that. Garrett is trending in the right direction, and McVay ’s comments make Australia the obvious target.
Still, the organization is drawing a firm line. The goal is to have Garrett ready for Week 1. The priority is making sure he is ready for everything that comes after it.

articles.title: Which NFL teams finished the preseason undefeated? Recent history offers a warning as we head into the 2026 season
articles.standfirst: Since 2021, only 10 of the 25 teams that remained unbeaten in pre-season made it to the play-offs
articles.summary: Since 2021, only 10 of the 25 teams that remained unbeaten in pre-season made it to the play-offs
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is right around the corner, and in the NFC , there is a clear favorite in the Los Angeles Rams , not only because Super Bowl 61 will be played at their home venue, SoFi Stadium where they captured their last Lombardi Trophy four seasons ago, or because they feature an elite offense led by reigning MVP Matthew Stafford , Puka Nacua , and Davante Adams .

The primary reason for their powerhouse status is their defense, bolstered by a blockbuster trade for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett , who is coming off a record-breaking sack campaign.

They also acquired star cornerback Trent McDuffie , alongside the stunning return of 3x Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald , who at 35 years old came out of retirement on a 1-year, $20 million deal to pair with Garrett in forming arguably the most terrifying pass-rushing duo in league history.

Preseason Perfection Meets History: Why Unbeaten Augusts Spell Danger for NFL Contenders

In theory, the biggest challengers to the Rams in the NFC are the defending champion Seattle Seahawks , but unlike the Rams, who swept their three preseason matchups against the Chiefs, Saints, and Chargers, the Seahawks failed to win a single exhibition contest while suffering more major roster departures than incoming signings during the offseason.

The Rams managed to finish the preseason undefeated alongside the Buffalo Bills , Baltimore Ravens , and Cincinnati Bengals . While all four squads look like heavy playoff locks on paper, recent history issues a stark warning.

Ever since the preseason slate was reduced from four games to three starting in 2021, 25 teams have finished the exhibition schedule undefeated, but only 10 of them managed to punch their ticket to the postseason, representing a modest 40% success rate .

Even more telling, out of those 25 unbeaten preseason squads, only the Denver Broncos managed to advance past the wild-card round last year.

For high-powered outfits like the Rams , Bills , Ravens , and Bengals , who are universally projected to contend for a Super Bowl title, the historical odds are strangely stacked against them. Looking closely at these trends, at least one of these four heavyweights is projected to miss the postseason entirely.

For the Bills and Rams , missing January football would register as an unmitigated disaster; for the Ravens , missing the playoffs in back-to-back seasons is something that has never occurred during the entire Lamar Jackson era; and for the Bengals , another postseason absence would mark four straight years without playoff football, applying immense pressure squarely onto Joe Burrow and the front office.
